description:
The standalone secondary-checkout deletion refusal becomes a case of the general
linked-checkout write policy rather than a parallel variant.

## Background

Issue deletion carries its own unconditional secondary-checkout refusal, checked independently
of any policy and with its own detection mechanism. With a general write policy governing
state-mutating dispatch, a second, private refusal for one command is exactly the parallel
variant the repository's convention-convergence invariant names a defect.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Deletion inside a linked non-primary checkout is governed by the general write policy, and the independent unconditional check no longer exists as a separate mechanism.
- [hard] REQ-02: Under the refusing stance, deletion inside a linked checkout keeps its current outcome: it is refused with an explanation before any write.
- [hard] REQ-03: Under a permitting stance or an explicit override, deletion follows the general policy like every other state-mutating invocation.
title: Converge the deletion refusal into the write policy
